query: Consider the following context: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for next-generation nuclear applications, particularly fusion reactors, due to their excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance. In that context, which material can be used for low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing the composition of refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can lead to the development of low-activation structural materials suitable for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors.
generation.intervention: Optimizing HEA composition for reduced activation and enhanced irradiation resistance
generation.mechanism: Alloy design for optimized properties, specifically low-activation and irradiation resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance, making HEAs suitable for low-activation structural material for high-temperature PFCs in fusion reactors
generation.baseline: Traditional materials with inadequate high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance
generation.boundary: Operating conditions of high-temperature fusion reactors
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition of HEAs that would achieve the desired properties is uncertain and requires further research

falsification_experiment.design: Experimental evaluation of optimized HEA compositions under high-temperature conditions in fusion reactors
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized HEA compositions do not exhibit improved high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance, and reduced activation levels, the hypothesis is falsified
